title: Speak vs. Know: Balancing Behavior and Knowledge Distributions of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27648v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work reports that the distribution verbalized directly in the output text aligns far better with human opinion distributions than the next-token log-probability distribution of LLMs. However, the verbalized distribution reflects what LLMs know about a group's opinions (knowledge distribution), while what they actually output at deployment is governed by their log-probability distribution (behavior distribution). We find that when prompting LLMs to predict the opinion of a specific group, the most likely answer under the verbalized distribution differs from that under the log-probability distribution for 37% of World Values Survey questions, averaged over three LLMs. Thus, LLMs' knowledge does not match their behavior. This matters for evaluation: a verbalized distribution can score well against a group while its most likely answer is one the model never outputs, so the score no longer describes the model. translated_title: 说与知：平衡大语言模型的行为分布与知识分布
translated_abstract: 最近的研究报告指出，直接在输出文本中表述出来的分布与人类意见分布的对齐程度，远优于大语言模型的下一个词元对数概率分布。然而，表述分布反映的是LLM对某一群体意见的“认知”（知识分布），而模型在部署时实际输出的内容则由其对数概率分布（行为分布）决定。我们发现，当提示LLM预测特定群体的意见时，在三个LLM上取平均，对于37%的世界价值观调查问题，表述分布下最可能的答案与对数概率分布下的最可能答案并不相同。因此，LLM的知识与其行为不匹配。这对评估意义重大：一个表述分布可以在与某群体意见的对比中获得高分，而其最可能的答案却是模型从不输出的内容，因此该分数不再能描述模型本身。
tldr: 论文揭示了大语言模型的“知识分布”（文本表述分布）与“行为分布”（对数概率分布）存在显著不一致——在37%的世界价值观调查问题上两者最可能的答案不同，导致基于表述分布的评估分数无法真实反映模型的实际行为，因而需要平衡这两种分布。
